description: Lakes are large bodies of water surrounded by land. Waterfalls are formed when a river falls steeply over a rocky ledge or cliff, holding immense ecological and economic significance in Geography.

sections.title: Major Types of Lakes
sections.description: Classification of lakes based on their origin and geographical structure.

key_concepts.explanation: Lakes formed due to the fracturing, faulting, or warping of the Earth's crust. Example: Wular Lake in Kashmir.
A lake formed when a volcanic crater or a caldera fills with water, or from a meteorite impact depression. Example: Lonar Lake in Maharashtra.
A shallow body of water separated from a larger body of water by barrier islands or coral reefs along the coast. Example: Chilika Lake in Odisha.
A U-shaped lake that forms when a wide meander of a river is cut off from the main channel, creating a free-standing body of water. Example: Kanwar Lake in Bihar.
